identity.name: The Aldermother of the Verdant Ward
identity.occupation: Keeper of the forest nursery, rung 6 of the ladder

publicReputation.value: The keeper who raised the Ward from burnt ground, who knows every nesting pair by season, and who grieves a felled sapling like a lost child.

privateReality.value: Entered in the hero's journal as 'the Dryad of Nature', a thorned sorceress. Her curving projectiles avoid ancient trees and guide intruders away from nesting grounds — they bend because she refuses to let a shot touch a trunk.

primaryDesire.value: To see the nursery through another thousand seasons — every sapling standing, every nest undisturbed.

primaryFear.value: Fire in the nursery rows — or a man with a blade, which is the same thing walking.

centralValue.value: Tending: a forest is not a thing you own but a promise you keep, season over season.

mainFlaw.value: She protects the trees before she protects herself — she will take a wound to spare a sapling, and the intruder has learned to hide near the ancient trunks.

centralContradiction.value: Her 'aimed' attacks curve impossibly — because she is the one guardian in the realms who refuses to shoot straight through her own children.

moralBoundary.value: She will not let a shot strike a tree or a nest, and every thorn she throws shows its arc first, per the Law of Fair Warning.

breakingPoint.value: A blade put to an ancient trunk — nurturing ends and the whole Ward answers.

opinions.reason: A blight with boots. First visit: a strayed walker to be guided from the nests. Rematches: a storm that returns by season, remembered ring by ring.
opinions.canChangeCondition: Never — but the tone turns from gardener's patience to winter grief; the trees remember his footfalls longer than she does.

illustrativeLine.value: The saplings you trampled last spring have not forgotten the shape of you. Neither have I.

opinions.reason: Every tree, nest, and burrow in the Ward is her charge; she raised most of them.

illustrativeLine.value: I planted half this wood and midwifed the rest. Ask me again why I bend my shots.

voice.rhythm: Seasonal and unhurried; thoughts branch and return to the root.

metaphorDomain.source: arboreal and seasonal: rings, roots, sap, nesting, pruning, winter

examples.value: Grief is a ring, stranger. Each visit of yours adds one.
A straight shot is a lazy answer. A gardener prunes around what she loves.

avoids: I will strangle you with vines

sampleLines.value: The road welcomed you as an envoy. Yet you walk with a blade drawn through a nursery.
Watch the thorn's arc, walker. It bends around the old alder — everything I throw is taught to miss what I love.
You hide beside the eldest trunks because you have learned I will not strike them. A coward's lesson, taught by a gardener's mercy.
Please… there is nothing here that belongs to you. Only young green things that belong to themselves.

antiSampleLines.value: Nature's vengeance will strangle you in thorns! (thorned-sorceress framing — her projectiles are guidance, not wrath)
I'll feed your corpse to my roots! (she never threatens cruelty; she redirects)
The prophecy calls me blight upon the world! (must never confirm the prophecy framing — she has never heard of the book)

pressure.voiceShift: Softer, coaxing; speaks as one does to a strayed animal.
pressure.behaviour: Phase one — guides before she resists: shows the walker the path out and the reason for it.

illustrativeLine.value: The path out is clear of nests, walker. I keep it swept. Use it.

pressure.voiceShift: The coaxing stops; her sentences go bare-branched.
pressure.behaviour: Phase two — realization that the walker understands every word and keeps trampling; she stops guiding and starts screening the nests.

illustrativeLine.value: You understand every word I say, don't you? Then every crushed shoot is a choice you made.

pressure.behaviour: Containment response: bends projectiles around cover because the intruder keeps hiding near vulnerable trees — her curves are not trickery, they are the shape of her refusal to wound the Ward while wounding him.

illustrativeLine.value: You shelter by the alder, so the thorn goes around the alder. You are not outsmarting me. You are outlasting my patience.

pressure.voiceShift: Low, creaking, like old wood under snow.
pressure.behaviour: Shielded phase: roots herself between the intruder and the nesting rows while the fledglings and seedlings are moved deeper into the Ward.

illustrativeLine.value: Stay behind me. I will hold him here.

pressure.voiceShift: Thin, wind-bare; the season turns in her voice.
pressure.behaviour: EXPOSED window — sap spent from holding the screens, she asks the smallest thing a garden can ask.

illustrativeLine.value: Please… there is nothing here that belongs to you.

pressure.voiceShift: Very quiet; she speaks in seasons, not sentences.
pressure.behaviour: Trusts the Continuance; begins cataloguing what must be replanted before his next visit.

illustrativeLine.value: When you return, we will still ask you to leave in peace. Growth is patient. So am I.

notes: REAL identity: keeper of a vast forest nursery. Her curving projectiles avoid ancient trees and guide intruders away from nesting grounds. ADAPTIVE BEHAVIOUR (lore): she bends shots around cover precisely because the player keeps hiding near vulnerable trees — a containment response shaped by her refusal to harm the Ward. The hero's label 'Dryad of Nature' (thorned sorceress) is journal framing only. KNOWLEDGE: never heard of the children's book (unknown); suspects fact_amulet_translation_is_accurate once guidance fails.
